2. Heard Sri Mohit Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Manish Pandey, learned counsel for the informant, Sri Jai Kishan Chaurasia, learned State Law Officer for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.172 of 2024, under Sections 376(2)N, 323, 504 and 506 I.P.C., Police Station Bahjoi, District Sambhal, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:

The applicant is stated to have established corporeal relationship with the victim for a period of about six months on the false promise of marriage and had subsequently refused to comply with the said betrothal.
5. The victim was found pregnant at that time.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
6. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
7. The said relationship was consensual as both were in love with each other.
8. The instant FIR has been instituted by the father of the victim after knowing about the pregnancy of his daughter.

9. The statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically indicates that she was in love with the applicant, although she has stated that the said corporeal relationship was established on the false promise of marriage and the applicant did not comply with the said promise.

10. The statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 03.05.2024 and subsequent to it, she had died on 19.05.2024 as se was found severely anemic and platelet count was also about 13000, as such, she died due to the complication she sustained.
11. The applicant has nothing to do with the said death and he has not been charged for it also.

12. The victim is major aged about 22 years as per the FIR itself and in the ossification test report,
her age has come out to be 20 years, as such, it stands corroborated to the FIR.
13.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
14. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 19.05.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/INFORMANT:
15. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:

has stated that entering into any kind of corporeal relationship with a person on the false promise to marry cannot be termed as rape.

The Supreme Court in the case of Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785 has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and Others, AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.
18. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

19. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
20.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
21.
?Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
22. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

23. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

24. Let the applicant- Kamal involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
Kamal vs State Of U.P. on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83023402/
3
( ii )

The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C/351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
25. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

26. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
